name: PhotoCraft
works_with: macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD and the web. AI agents can drive it through a CLI or an MCP server
short: A free, open-source photo editor in pure Rust that works like Photoshop and opens and saves real PSD files.
what: PhotoCraft is a clean-room reimplementation of Photoshop written in Rust. It has layers, masks, 16 adjustment layers, layer styles, editable type, vector shapes, a brush engine and 67 tools, and it opens and saves layered PSD files. Every menu item is a command, so a script or an AI agent can run the same edits through `photocraft-cli` or its MCP server.
who: Anyone who wants a free Photoshop-style editor that runs offline, and developers who want to batch-edit images or let an agent do it. The team says it is early alpha and not yet ready to replace Photoshop for daily professional work.
needs: To install: a download for your system from the getartcraft.com PhotoCraft page or the GitHub releases
To build from source: git and Rust's `cargo`
Optional: the craft-fonts repo for Japanese fonts in source builds

steps.title: Download it
steps.text: The easiest route is the PhotoCraft page on getartcraft.com. The latest GitHub release has every build: `.msi` or portable zip for Windows, a signed `.dmg` for macOS, AppImage, Flatpak, `.deb`, `.rpm` or tarball for Linux, plus FreeBSD and web builds. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for each file.

steps.title: Or install the Flatpak on Linux
steps.code:
flatpak install --user photocraft-<version>-linux-x86_64.flatpak   # or -linux-aarch64
flatpak run ai.storyteller.photocraft

steps.title: Or build it from source
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/storytold/photocraft
cd photocraft
cargo run --release -p photocraft -- image.psd   # the desktop app
cargo test --workspace                           # the test suite

steps.title: Edit from the command line
steps.text: `photocraft-cli` runs the same commands headless, on one file or a folder. Every subcommand has `--help`.

steps.title: Let an agent drive it
steps.text: This starts the MCP server, headless or bridged to the running app.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Use the README's headless example: open `wave.psd` with `photocraft-cli run`, add Smart Sharpen and a Curves adjustment layer, and save it as `wave-final.png`.

watch: It's early alpha. The README says the biggest gaps are AI and generative features, 15 missing tools, typography depth and plug-in support.
A re-saved PSD renders the same in almost all of their tests, but the file isn't byte-identical to the original. Keep a copy of important files.
The AppImage registers a launcher and menu entry in `~/.local/share` on first run. Set `PHOTOCRAFT_NO_DESKTOP_INTEGRATION=1` to skip that.
On Wayland, dropping files on the window doesn't open them yet. Use File › Open or paste with Ctrl+V.
The desktop app has a control channel (`photocraft --control`) that can drive tools and take screenshots. It is authenticated and listens only on your own machine.
